cues.zh: 如果你在给某家公司打电话等待接通，而他们通过电话为你播放音乐，
cues.en: If you're on hold to a company, and they're playing music down the phone at you,

cues.zh: 那音乐很可能听起来很糟糕，有时甚至会变成一片杂音。
cues.en: the chances are it sounds terrible, and sometimes it just dissolves into static.

cues.zh: 电话信号的用途并不是传输音乐，而要解释原因，
cues.en: Telephone signals are not designed to carry music, and to explain why,

cues.zh: 我们得从很早很早以前说起，从像这样的老式电话设备讲起。
cues.en: we have to start way, way back with old telephone equipment like this.

cues.zh: 早期的电话通话是由人工接线员接通的，
cues.en: Early telephone calls were put through by a human operator

cues.zh: 接线员会在一个大型开关板上，
cues.en: who would be literally connecting the two phone wires into one circuit

cues.zh: 把两根电话线实际连接到同一个电路里。
cues.en: at a big board of switches.

cues.zh: 也就是所谓的“交换机”。
cues.en: Or a "switchboard".

cues.zh: 一端发出的任何声音，无论是语音、音乐还是别的什么，
cues.en: Any sound at one end, whether it's speech, music, whatever,

cues.zh: 都会被转换成电信号，沿线路发送出去，
cues.en: would be converted to an electrical signal, sent down the wire,

cues.zh: 然后在另一端再转换回来。
cues.en: and converted back at the other end.

cues.zh: 你发送音乐，就会收到音乐——
cues.en: You send music, you receive music --

cues.zh: 尽管音质会受到微型麦克风和扬声器性能的限制。
cues.en: although it'd be limited by the abilities of the tiny microphone and speaker.

cues.zh: 但像这样的电话交换机只适用于少量连接。
cues.en: But telephone exchanges like this only work for small numbers of connections.

cues.zh: 因为显然，你不可能每通电话都这么接。
cues.en: Because, you know, you can't do this for every call.

cues.zh: 电话公司很快意识到，他们可以省下
cues.en: Phone companies quickly realised that they could save

cues.zh: 在相隔数英里的交换机之间铺设数千条线路的成本，
cues.en: on setting up thousands of wires between exchanges miles apart

cues.zh: 只要他们能在一根线上同时传输多路通话。
cues.en: if they were able to put several conversations down one wire at the same time.

cues.zh: 因此，与其传输原始信号中的所有声音频率，
cues.en: So rather than transmit every frequency of sound in the original signal,

cues.zh: 他们选择切掉高频和低频，
cues.en: they would cut off the high and low frequencies,

cues.zh: 也就是那些我们听懂语音并不绝对需要的频段，
cues.en: the ones we don't absolutely need to understand speech,

cues.zh: 然后把每路通话移到不同的频段上。
cues.en: and then they would shift each call into a different frequency band.

cues.zh: 在另一端，就像调收音机一样，
cues.en: At at the other end, like tuning in a radio,

cues.zh: 他们再把每路通话调回原本的频率，让你能听清楚。
cues.en: they would shift each call back to the right frequencies so you could hear it.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，音质算不上多好，但也足够用了。
cues.en: I mean, the quality wasn't great, but it was good enough.

cues.zh: 而且，我们还拥有了廉价的长途电话。
cues.en: And hey, we got cheap long distance calling.

cues.zh: 我们习惯了那种电话音质的声音。
cues.en: We got used to that phone-quality sound.

cues.zh: 它成了标准。
cues.en: And it became the standard.

cues.zh: 所以，[电话铃声] 音乐听起来已经有点问题了，
cues.en: So already [PHONE RINGS] music was going to sound a bit dodgy,

cues.zh: 所有高频和低频都被切掉了。
cues.en: with all the high and low frequencies cut off.

cues.zh: 但当我们还在模拟电路上运行时，
cues.en: But while we were still running on analogue circuits

cues.zh: 它不会听起来像静电噪音。
cues.en: it wasn't going to sound like static.

cues.zh: 那是计算机的错。
cues.en: That was the fault of computers.

cues.zh: 电话公司意识到，他们可以在同一根线上发送更多通话，
cues.en: Phone companies realised that they could send even more calls down the same wire,

cues.zh: 或者在蜂窝网络的同一空域中，
cues.en: or into the same airspace on a cellular network,

cues.zh: 如果他们用计算机来压缩音频。
cues.en: if they used computers to compress the audio.

cues.zh: 他们压缩得越多，
cues.en: And the more they compressed it,

cues.zh: 同一时间就能容纳越多通话，
cues.en: the more calls they could fit at the same time,

cues.zh: 对他们来说就越便宜。
cues.en: and the cheaper it'd be for them.

cues.zh: 如今，几乎每个人的手机都有足够的算力
cues.en: These days, there is enough power in pretty much everyone's phone

cues.zh: 实时压缩4K视频，但那时候，还远远不够。
cues.en: to compress 4K video in real time, but back then, not so much.

cues.zh: MP3才刚刚被发明出来，而且它们的算力不够
cues.en: MP3s had only just been invented, and these do not have enough power

cues.zh: 去压缩那些音频。
cues.en: to compress those.

cues.zh: 电话通话的标准，甚至到今天，仍然依赖于快速粗糙的压缩
cues.en: The standards for phone calls, even today, rely on quick-and-dirty compression

cues.zh: 那是几十年前构建的，设计用于在极低的计算能力上运行，
cues.en: built decades ago, designed to run on very little computing power,

cues.zh: 并且针对语音进行了优化。
cues.en: and optimised for speech.

cues.zh: 这种压缩在编码一个清晰的声音时非常出色——
cues.en: That compression is great at encoding one clear voice --

cues.zh: 但把大量复杂的音乐扔给它，带着各种乐器
cues.en: but chuck a load of complicated music at it, with all its instruments

cues.zh: [压缩后的音乐] 听起来就会很糟糕。
cues.en: [COMPRESSED MUSIC] and it's going to sound bad.

cues.zh: 但还不至于糟糕到变成静电噪音。
cues.en: But not quite enough to break down into static.

cues.zh: 还有最后一块拼图。
cues.en: There is one last piece of the puzzle.

cues.zh: 又有人偷工减料了。
cues.en: Someone else cutting corners.

cues.zh: 因为最坏的情况下，那段等待音乐不仅仅是被压缩了
cues.en: Because in the worst case, that hold music isn’t just compressed

cues.zh: 在电话公司传给你的路上。
cues.en: by the phone company on its way to you.

cues.zh: 它已经被一个完全不同的系统压缩过了
cues.en: It’s already been compressed by a completely different system

cues.zh: 当你的通话在公司内部电话网络中来回传递时。
cues.en: as your call bounces around a company’s internal phone network.

cues.zh: 内部电话网络大概率还是由中标价最低的承包商建的。
cues.en: An internal phone network that has probably been built by the lowest bidder.

cues.zh: 于是电话公司拿到了这串已经被压烂的信号，
cues.en: So the phone company takes that already-mangled signal

cues.zh: 在把它传给你的路上，又用另一种方式蹂躏了一遍。
cues.en: and mangles it in a different way as it travels to you.

cues.zh: 要是系统设计得特别烂，
cues.en: And in a really badly designed system,

cues.zh: 可能还会套上第三层糟糕透顶的压缩，
cues.en: maybe there’s an entire third layer of terrible compression

cues.zh: 这来自运营呼叫中心的其他公司，
cues.en: from whichever other company runs the call centre

cues.zh: 而你实际上正跟他们隔着重洋通话。
cues.en: that you're actually talking to, off in some other country.

cues.zh: [音乐渐强] 语音尚且能在这种链路里撑下来，
cues.en: [MUSIC RISES] Speech can survive that chain

cues.zh: 但音乐……
cues.en: But music...

cues.zh: [音乐变成杂音] ……音乐可撑不住！
cues.en: [MUSIC TURNS TO STATIC] ...music can't!

cues.zh: 非常感谢 Milton Keynes Museum 的全体团队，
cues.en: Thank you so much to all the team at the Milton Keynes Museum

cues.zh: 以及他们的 Connected Earth 展厅，
cues.en: and their Connected Earth gallery,

cues.zh: 这里几乎所有的电话交换设备
cues.en: where pretty much all this telephone exchange equipment

cues.zh: 都可以直接上手随便玩。
cues.en: is just open to play around with.

cues.zh: 想了解更多关于他们的信息，请看简介栏。
cues.en: Pull down the description for more about them.

cues.zh: 这不是塔迪斯。
cues.en: This is not a TARDIS.

cues.zh: 这实际上就是个警用电话亭。
cues.en: This is literally just a police telephone box.
